historic_survey.finding: Appears eligible for the California Register under Criterion 1 (the earliest development of Glen Park) and Criterion 3 (architecture)
historic_survey.note: The finding is the San Francisco Planning Department's, from its own survey of the parcels west of Lippard Avenue and inside the neighborhood commercial zoning, which this evaluation reprints. The dairyman William Tietz built it in 1872, when Glen Park was dairy, pig and vegetable farms on the old Rancho San Miguel and its homesteads did not line up with the street grid imposed in the 1890s. A small gabled cottage with wood shingle cladding, standing about twenty feet back from the street.

building.completed_conflict: The evaluation dates the house to 1872 and the assessor's roll to 1900.
